subject: Archaeology
title: Tomb Robbers of Ancient Egypt
description: A quick win: understand Tomb Robbers of Ancient Egypt.

hook.text: Almost every pharaoh's tomb was robbed in antiquity. The thieves were often the workers who built them.

buildup.text: Ancient court records describe tomb robbery trials during the reign of Ramesses IX, around 1100 BCE.

discovery.text: Confessions reveal teams who tunneled through rock at night and melted down golden coffins for resale.

twist.text: Corrupt officials sometimes protected the robbers in exchange for a share of the loot.

climax.text: Priests eventually moved royal mummies to secret caches to protect them. Over 50 were hidden in one cave.

punchline.text: The pharaohs' best security was a cave nobody could find.

quiz.question: How did priests ultimately protect royal mummies from thieves?
options: They placed armed guards at every tomb entrance
They moved the mummies to secret hidden caches
They cursed the tombs with magical inscriptions

details.summary: Tomb robbery was a persistent problem throughout Egyptian history despite elaborate security measures. Ancient court records document organized gangs of workers who tunneled into royal tombs, melted down gold artifacts, and bribed officials to avoid punishment.
details.whyItMatters: Tomb robbery explains why Tutankhamun's intact tomb was so extraordinary — virtually every other royal tomb was looted in antiquity. Understanding ancient theft also explains gaps in the archaeological record.
takeaways: Tomb robbery was organized crime in ancient Egypt
Ancient court records document trials of tomb robbers
Nearly every royal tomb was looted before modern excavation

faq.question: How do we know about ancient tomb robbery?
faq.answer: Papyrus court records from the reign of Ramesses IX document formal trials of tomb robbers. Workers confessed to breaking into tombs, stripping gold from coffins, and dividing the loot. These texts reveal organized criminal networks operating over generations.

faq.question: What security measures did Egyptians use to protect tombs?
faq.answer: Measures included hidden entrances, false chambers, sealed corridors filled with rubble, and dedicated tomb police patrols. The Valley of the Kings itself was chosen for its remote, guarded location. Despite all this, almost every tomb was eventually robbed.
